about: Assembly rules for Lordaeron timber-frame homes, shops and terraces. Pure data: a deterministic function of the params below. The reference assembler (assemble.mjs, delivered beside this file) implements exactly these rules; diff your C16's output against it block for block.

params.trade: null, or a workstation block id placed for the occupant ("any" leaves a marker for the placer)
params.units: terraces only: a list of widths, built side by side sharing party walls

constraints: roof gable_z (gable to the street) needs width 5 or 7: its roof slices span the width
front jettied needs depth 7 and storeys 2
expressions: Positions are [x, y, z] in the template, origin at its north-west corner on the lowest layer, front to the south. Each coordinate is an integer or an expression over: W (width), D (depth), c = (W-1)/2 (the door's x), g (the storey's floor layer), zw (the front wall's z: D-1, or D-2 on a jettied ground storey), zf = zw-1 (the front room's row), storeys. Operators + - * /, comparisons, && ||; integer arithmetic.

grid.storey_base: g = 2 + 4 * s for storey s = 0, 1; layer g is the sill and floor, g+1..g+3 the room

foundation.at: every cell of the footprint, layers 0-1

floor.at: every cell inside the walls at layer g, each storey; under a jetty, the street strip at layer 2 is foundation-topped paving (plinth)

front_back.rule: the centre column is the feature; outward from it, columns repeat panel, panel, stud; the ends are corners. On a ground-storey front 7 or wider, the columns either side of the door are studs (jambs) and the repeat starts after them.
front_back.windows: the panels of pair j are windows when j is even (j = floor((k'-1)/3), k' = distance from the centre, less one after door jambs); on the back, ground-storey pairs stay plain
front_back.shop: front shop: the ground storey's pair j = 0 is shop (wide glazing) instead of window

sides.rule: outward from each corner, columns repeat panel, panel, stud; a side of odd length has a window at its centre

chimney.stack: chimney_stack from roof_base to roof_base + layers (one above the ridge)

jetty.street_strip: z = D-1 at the ground storey: open, paved, under the upper storey
jetty.brackets: jetty_bracket at [x, g+3, D-1] of the ground storey under every post_corner and stud of the upper front wall
jetty.lantern: lantern at [c, g+3, D-1] of the ground storey, hanging from the upper sill

roof.layers: (span-1)/2 + 1, the first on the walls' top

ground.note: rises through a hole in the upper floor
beside a bed's head, clear of every way in
hanging; one more at c-4 and c+4 when W >= 9

fitout.rules: Beds and workstations only on the ground storey, so a villager walks to them from the door with no stairs. Nothing that is a point of interest except declared beds and workstations. No chest touches a workstation.

terrace.rule: units side by side from the west, each sharing its west wall with the previous unit's east wall (a unit of width w adds w-1); each unit is a home with its own door, beds, hearth and chimney; one continuous gable_x roof with gable ends at both ends of the row and gable_end slices on every party wall

palette: Parts are authored in the base palette (stone). To apply another, replace each block by the palette's block for the same role (palettes.json); stairs, slabs and doors keep their states, full blocks drop them.
pick: Deterministic: the placer chooses params from the town and the slot (e.g. palette from the slot's position, a seeded hash of town id and slot). These rules never choose at random.
